Definition: from G435 and G3534; man of victory; Andronicos, an Israelite:--Adronicus.
BiblicalUsage: Andronicus appears once, in Paul's greetings, as his kinsman and fellow prisoner, of note among the apostles, and in Christ before Paul was. One verse gives him a whole history: kin, prison, honour, and an earlier faith than Paul's own.
TheologicalSignificance: A man known from a single greeting still shows me something real: faithfulness before fame, prison shared with an apostle, and a name Paul thought worth remembering.
